title: Belonging and Inclusion
summary: أهم كلمات Unit 9 (Circles of Belonging) عن الانتماء والعلاقات والدمج والمجتمع، بالمعنى الإنجليزي والعربي وأمثلة وتدريبات زي Review E.

blocks.text: الدرس ده عن إيه؟

text: This page collects the **key vocabulary of Unit 9: Circles of Belonging**. Each word has a simple English meaning, the Arabic meaning and a short example. Then you will practise word families, collocations, prefixes and suffixes, synonyms and antonyms.

blocks.text: الصفحة دي فيها **أهم كلمات Unit 9: Circles of Belonging**، متقسمة حسب دروس الوحدة. الوحدة بتتكلم عن **الإحساس بالانتماء (belonging)**: إنك تحس إن الناس شايفاك ومقدّراك، وعن **العلاقات اللي بتخليك تكبر (growth relationships)**، و**الدمج (inclusion)** علشان محدش يحس إنه متساب لوحده، وإزاي **المجتمع (community)** بيتحرك يساعد ناسه.

الكلمات دي متاخدة من نصوص الوحدة وجداول الـ **Vocabulary** و**Media Analysis: Key Concepts** في الكتاب: **9.1 Finding My Place** (قصة طالبة جديدة)، **9.2 Relationships That Help Us Grow** (The People Who Shape Us)، **9.3 No One Left Behind** (الـ Buddy Bench)، **9.4 Community That Cares** (ثريد CommunityCaresEG)، وكمان **Consolidation Review E**.
إزاي تذاكر الكلمات صح؟

text: Do not learn a word alone. Learn its **meaning in context**, its **family** (noun, verb, adjective, adverb) and the words that usually go **with** it (collocations).

blocks.text: أسئلة الكتاب والمراجعات مش بتسألك «ترجم الكلمة» وخلاص. بتحطلك الكلمة **جوه جملة** وتسألك معناها **في السياق ده** (What does … mean in this context?)، أو تطلب منك **تغيّر شكل الكلمة** (noun / adjective / adverb)، أو تطلع **مرادف أو عكس** من قطعة. علشان كده ذاكر كل كلمة بالطريقة دي:

items: **اقرا المثال الأول** وافهم الكلمة من الجملة قبل ما تبص على الترجمة.
**احفظ المعنى الإنجليزي البسيط**، لأن الاختيارات في الـ MCQ بتيجي تعريفات بالإنجليزي.
**اعرف عيلة الكلمة**: الاسم والفعل والصفة والظرف.
**اعرف الكلمة بتيجي مع إيه** (collocation) زي feel left out مش feel left.
**اكتب جملة بنفسك** عن موضوع الوحدة بكل كلمة جديدة. الكتاب بيطلب كده في Practice: Write FOUR sentences using words from the text.

blocks.text: كلمات 9.1: Finding My Place
طالبة اتنقلت من إسكندرية لمدينة جديدة في نص الترم، وكانت بتاكل لوحدها أسبوعين، لحد ما زميلة ساعدتها في الجنينة وبدأت تحس بالانتماء.

items: belonging
الانتماء · the feeling of being accepted and valued as part of a group · مثال: **Belonging** is built through small moments.
basic human need
احتياج إنساني أساسي · something every person needs, like food and safety · مثال: Psychologists call belonging a **basic human need**.
luxury
رفاهية · something special that is nice but not necessary · مثال: Belonging is a need, not a **luxury**.
unseen
مش ملحوظ / محدش شايفه · not noticed by others · مثال: A student who feels **unseen** stops raising their hand.
withdraw
ينسحب / يبعد · to stop taking part or pull back · مثال: Lonely students often **withdraw** from activities.
afterthought
حاجة جت على البال بعدين · something you think about and add later · مثال: She asked about my old school as an **afterthought**.
crack open a door
يفتح باب (فرصة) · to make something possible to happen · مثال: One conversation **cracked open a door**.
assignment
واجب / تكليف · work that a teacher asks students to do · مثال: She helped me with a biology **assignment**.
stranger
غريب · a person you do not know · مثال: I felt like a **stranger** in my own country.
setback
انتكاسة / عقبة · a problem that stops progress for a time · مثال: People who belong recover faster from **setbacks**.
fit in
يندمج / يتأقلم مع المجموعة · to be accepted by a group · مثال: Belonging is not about **fitting in** perfectly.
connection
علاقة / صلة · a relationship between people · مثال: Even one **connection** can say "You are seen here."

blocks.text: كلمات 9.2: Relationships That Help Us Grow
التسجيل بيشرح الـ **growth relationship**: علاقة مش بس بتونسك، لا دي بتخليك أقدر وأثقف وأقوى.

items: growth relationship
علاقة بتنمّيك · a relationship that helps a person become more capable and confident · مثال: A good teacher can build a **growth relationship**.
transformative
بيغيّر بشكل كبير (للأحسن) · causing a major positive change · مثال: Peer support can be **transformative**.
mentor
مرشد / موجّه · an experienced person who guides someone less experienced · مثال: My **mentor** reviewed my essay.
peer
زميل في نفس السن · a person of the same age or social status · مثال: **Peers** can help as much as adults.
encouragement
تشجيع · support that helps someone succeed · مثال: Her **encouragement** gave me confidence.
consistency
الثبات / الانتظام · behaving in the same reliable way over time · مثال: **Consistency** is more powerful than one kind comment.
resilient
قوي / بيقوم بسرعة بعد الصعوبات · able to recover quickly from difficulties · مثال: Honest feedback made her more **resilient**.
empty praise
مدح فاضي (من غير معنى) · praise that is not honest or useful · مثال: A good mentor avoids **empty praise**.
allow for failure
يسمح بالغلط · to let someone make mistakes and learn · مثال: Good mentors **allow for failure**.
capable
قادر / كفء · able to do things well · مثال: Support helps people feel more **capable**.

blocks.text: كلمات 9.3: No One Left Behind
النص عن **الـ Buddy Bench**: دكة في ملعب مدرسة في القاهرة، اللي يقعد عليها يبقى معناه «عايز حد يلعب معايا».

items: social inclusion
الدمج الاجتماعي · making sure everyone feels noticed, valued and welcome · مثال: **Social inclusion** starts with small actions.
exclusion
الاستبعاد / العزل · the state of being left out · مثال: Quiet **exclusion** is hard to notice.
left out
متساب لوحده / مستبعد · not included in a group or activity · مثال: No child should feel **left out**.
invisible
مش مرئي (محدش واخد باله منه) · not seen or noticed, even when present · مثال: A lonely student can feel **invisible**.
overlook
يتجاهل / ما ياخدش باله · to fail to notice something or someone · مثال: Loneliness is easy to **overlook**.
courage
شجاعة · the ability to do something difficult or frightening · مثال: Inclusion should need no **courage**.
structured
منظم (ليه نظام) · carefully organised with a clear plan · مثال: Some students need **structured** support.
low-pressure
من غير ضغط · not causing stress or a feeling of being forced · مثال: The bench is a **low-pressure** signal.
initiative
مبادرة · a new plan or action to solve a problem · مثال: The Buddy Bench is a simple **initiative**.
isolation
عزلة · being alone and separated from others · مثال: Playground **isolation** dropped in one term.
loneliness
الوحدة · the sad feeling of being alone · مثال: The bench fights the quiet **loneliness** of children.
supplement
يكمّل / يدعم · to add to something to make it better · مثال: Small ideas **supplement** professional counselling.

blocks.text: كلمات 9.4: Community That Cares
ثريد عن 3 أصحاب بدأوا يجمعوا تبرعات من جيرانهم، وبقوا شبكة من 200 متطوع في 4 محافظات ساعدوا أهالي المنيا بعد الأمطار.

items: civic engagement
المشاركة المجتمعية · actions people take to improve their community · مثال: Volunteering is a form of **civic engagement**.
grassroots initiative
مبادرة شعبية (من الناس نفسها) · an effort organised by ordinary people, not official institutions · مثال: It began as a small **grassroots initiative**.
mutual aid
المساعدة المتبادلة · community members supporting each other directly · مثال: **Mutual aid** reached 40 households.
mobilise
يحشد / يجمّع الناس بسرعة · to organise people quickly for a shared purpose · مثال: Social media helps people **mobilise** support. (الكتاب بيكتبها mobilize)
urgent
عاجل · needing immediate action · مثال: Families had an **urgent** need for blankets.
respond (to)
يستجيب لـ / يرد · to react to a situation, often with help · مثال: Volunteers **responded** quickly **to** the crisis.
dramatically
بشكل كبير جدًا · in a way that involves a big, noticeable change · مثال: Community connection has changed **dramatically**.
connected
مترابط · having strong social links with others · مثال: People feel more **connected** than before.
correct (verb)
يصحّح · to fix a mistake · مثال: Two networks had to **correct** false addresses.
official channels
الجهات الرسمية · government offices and registered organisations · مثال: Help used to come only through **official channels**.
word of mouth
الكلام من شخص لشخص · information passed on by people talking · مثال: Everything was organised by **word of mouth**.

blocks.text: عيلة الكلمة (Word Families)

text: Many questions ask for **the correct form of the word in brackets**. Learn the noun, verb, adjective and adverb together.

blocks.text: الجدول ده فيه أشهر عيلات الكلمات في الوحدة. خلي بالك من الزوج **include / exclude** لأنهم عكس بعض:
إزاي أعرف محتاج أنهي شكل من الكلمة؟

text: Look at the word **before** and **after** the gap. The position tells you if you need a noun, a verb, an adjective or an adverb.

blocks.text: في سؤال **Complete the sentences using the correct form of the word in brackets** بص على مكان الفراغ:
كلمات بتيجي مع بعض (Collocations)

text: A **collocation** is a group of words that native speakers usually use together. Using them makes your writing sound natural.

blocks.text: الـ collocation يعني كلمتين «متجوزين»: لازم تستخدمهم مع بعض. احفظهم كده:

rows: Clubs help students **feel a sense of belonging**.
يخلّي حد يحس إنه مرحّب بيه
A smile can **make someone feel welcome**.
Students who belong **take more risks** in class.
**Reach out to** someone who sits alone.
Volunteers **responded to the crisis** in Minya.
Neighbours **made donations** of food and blankets.
The group grew into a **support network**.

blocks.text: البادئات واللواحق (Prefixes & Suffixes)

text: A **prefix** comes at the start of a word and often changes its meaning. A **suffix** comes at the end and often changes the word class (noun, adjective…).

blocks.text: الـ **prefix** في **أول** الكلمة، والـ **suffix** في **آخرها**:
المرادفات والأضداد (Synonyms & Antonyms)

text: Reviews ask you to give words from a text that could **replace** given words, or to choose the **opposite** in meaning.

blocks.text: فقرة بالكلمات الجديدة
اقرا الفقرة دي وركّز على الكلمات اللي بالـ bold. كلها من الوحدة:

text: When Adam joined a new school in Tanta, he felt like a **stranger**. He sat alone at break, and slowly he began to **withdraw** from class activities. He felt **unseen**, almost **invisible**, although nobody was **unkind** to him. His classmates simply **overlooked** him.

Everything changed when a **peer** invited him to the school's reading club, almost as an **afterthought**. That small invitation **cracked open a door**. The club leader became a **mentor** who **offered encouragement** but never **empty praise**. With her **consistency** and honest feedback, Adam became more **resilient**. By the end of the year, he was helping other new students so that no one would **feel left out**. For Adam, **belonging** was not a **luxury**: it was a **basic human need**.

blocks.text: لاحظ: الفقرة فيها collocations زي **offered encouragement** و**feel left out**، وفيها كلمات بنفس المعنى (unseen / invisible) علشان تتعود عليها في سؤال الـ replace.

blocks.title: أشهر الأخطاء (غلط ← صح)
items: ✗ I feel belong here. ← ✓ I feel **a sense of belonging** here. / I **belong** here.
✗ I belong the team. ← ✓ I belong **to** the team. (belong محتاجة to)
✗ The bench encouraged greater include. ← ✓ The bench encouraged greater **inclusion**. (بعد صفة = اسم)
✗ empty praise = تشجيع حقيقي ← ✓ empty praise = **مدح فاضي** مالوش قيمة، والمراجعة بتسأل عليها
✗ lonely (ظرف) ← ✓ lonely **صفة** رغم إنها آخرها -ly: He felt lonely.
✗ respond the message ← ✓ respond **to** the message

blocks.title: حيلة سريعة للحفظ وللامتحان
items: **in**clusion = جوه المجموعة، **ex**clusion = برّه المجموعة (زي exit = خروج).
اعرف **عكس invisible** في الامتحان: recognised / visible / noticed (مش isolated ولا ignored).
اربط الكلمة بالنص: **afterthought / crack open a door** = الطالبة الجديدة، **Buddy Bench / low-pressure** = 9.3، **mutual aid / grassroots** = الثريد.

blocks.text: إزاي بييجي في الأسئلة؟
الأسئلة في الكتاب والمراجعات بتيجي بالأشكال دي. هنحل مثال لكل شكل:
**1) Which word is the opposite in meaning?**

text: Quiet exclusion can leave a student physically present but socially invisible. Which word is the opposite in meaning to "invisible"?
a. isolated   b. ignored   c. recognised   d. excluded

blocks.text: **الإجابة: c. recognised.** الاختيارات التانية كلها **قريبة** من معنى invisible أو exclusion، وده الفخ.
**2) Complete the sentence using the correct form of the word in brackets.**

text: The organisers checked every claim to improve the ________ (rely) of the campaign.

blocks.text: **الإجابة: reliability.** بعد the وقبل of محتاجين **اسم**.
**3) Give words or phrases from the text that could meaningfully replace the meanings in the box.**

text: A new student may feel unseen and begin to withdraw from group activities.
Meanings: (a) not noticed by others   (b) stop taking part or pull back

blocks.text: **الإجابة:** (a) **unseen** (b) **withdraw**. هنا السؤال بيدّيك **التعريف** وانت تطلع **الكلمة** من القطعة.
تدريب
**A. Choose the correct answer from a, b, c or d.**

items.q:
1. A supportive mentor can be transformative because she changes how a student sees their abilities. "Transformative" means ________.
a. requiring little effort  b. causing an important positive change  c. staying the same  d. hard to recognise

2. A person of the same age or social status as another is called a ________.
a. consumer  b. mentor  c. peer  d. organiser

3. Direct support exchanged among members of a community is known as ________.
a. mass production  b. mutual aid  c. luxury  d. exclusion

4. A sense of belonging often develops gradually. The opposite of "gradually" is ________.
a. slowly  b. suddenly  c. quietly  d. carefully

5. After the floods, three friends organised help without waiting for official channels. Their effort was a ________.
a. structured programme  b. grassroots initiative  c. luxury  d. setback
items.a: **b. grassroots initiative** — مبادرة من الناس العادية.

items.q:
6. The teacher said, "Well done!" to every answer, even wrong ones. This is an example of ________.
a. honest feedback  b. empty praise  c. civic engagement  d. consistency
items.a: **b. empty praise** — مدح من غير ما يساعد الطالب يتحسن.

items.q:
7. Honest feedback helped Mariam recover quickly from her mistakes. She became more ________.
a. resilient  b. invisible  c. urgent  d. isolated

blocks.text: **B. Complete the sentences using the correct form of the word in brackets.**

items.q: 8. The Buddy Bench encouraged greater ________ (include) among students who felt left out.
items.a: **inclusion** — بعد الصفة greater اسم (سؤال زي Review E).

items.q: 9. A teacher's ________ (encourage) can change a student's future.
10. Volunteers acted ________ (urgent) when the rain destroyed homes.
11. Many new students suffer from ________ (lonely) in their first weeks.
12. Social media has ________ (dramatic) changed how communities help each other.
13. Schools should be ________ (include) places where every student feels welcome.

blocks.text: **C. Give words or phrases from the text that could meaningfully replace the meanings below.**

text: On his first day, Ziad felt invisible. Classmates were not unkind, but they overlooked him, and he began to pull back from group work. Then a classmate invited him to the football team. That small gesture opened a door to a new friendship. Within a month, Ziad felt accepted and valued as part of the team.

items.q: 14. not seen or noticed by others, even when present
15. failed to notice someone
16. stop taking part (a phrasal verb)
17. made something new possible (a phrase)
items.a: **opened a door** — زي crack open a door.

items.q: 18. a sense of belonging
items.a: **felt accepted and valued as part of the team**

blocks.text: **D. Complete the sentences using words from the box.**

text: luxury – afterthought – low-pressure – mobilise – mentor – setbacks

items.q: 19. Psychologists describe belonging as a basic need, not a ________.
20. She asked about my old school almost as an ________.
21. The bench is a ________ way to ask for company: you just sit down.
22. Social media helps ordinary people ________ support very quickly.
23. My ________ guided me and reviewed my work every week.
24. Students who feel they belong recover faster from ________.

blocks.title: ملخص الدرس في سطرين
items: كلمات الوحدة بتدور حول: **الانتماء** (belonging, unseen, withdraw, afterthought)، **العلاقات** (mentor, peer, resilient, empty praise)، **الدمج** (inclusion ↔ exclusion, invisible, overlook, low-pressure) و**المجتمع** (mutual aid, grassroots, mobilise).
احفظ العيلات: include → inclusion → inclusive / encourage → encouragement / rely → reliability → reliable.
عكس **invisible** = recognised / visible. عكس **gradually** = suddenly. عكس **luxury** = necessity.
في سؤال **replace** السؤال بيدّيك التعريف وانت تطلع الكلمة من القطعة.
